status: Capabilities vary by format; inspect each operation and its functional limits.

layers.label: DOCX
layers.engine: SuperDoc SDK 2.2.1 / v2 plus guarded OOXML adapters; optional Word/LibreOffice layout
layers.summary: 14 agent-facing DOCX tools backed by SuperDoc v2, durable candidates, semantic/package validation and durable PDF export.
layers.limitations: Optional layout providers supply revision-bound page text targets and explicit Word-reference appearance comparisons. Guarded textbox/equation/chart edits and merged/nested cell text are supported within their declared limits. Full table reconstruction, style definitions and some complex tracked ranges remain incomplete.
missing: Reliable tracked edits in all formatted/table-bearing documents
Page targeting of ambiguous text, cross-page ranges and opaque objects
Unrestricted nested-table reconstruction and arbitrary object authoring
Guaranteed fresh page fields across Word-compatible renderers
layers.proposedEngine: SuperDoc remains the only mutation engine. Independent package checks are read-only evidence; LibreOffice is used only for PDF export.

evaluation.summary: Open/create, canonical reads, semantic query, guarded actions, validation and save/export are available. Run test:response for semantic/package acceptance; application display testing is separate.

operations.name: docx_open
operations.description: Open one allowed DOCX source and return a revision-bound view. Opening inventories the file but does not claim that every story or visual page was read.

Optional operator-supplied Word PDF reference compares exact pixels for this revision, without claiming universal Word equivalence.

operations.name: docx_inspect
operations.description: Without view, discover actions/workflows and examples without opening a document. With view, also return document counts, outline, diagnostics and a reading plan. Request actions, actionFamily or workflows for focused schemas.

actionFamily.description: Select a family from actionFamilies to return only its action names and at most 20 exact argument schemas. An explicit actions list overrides the family descriptor selection.

actions.description: Return machine-readable descriptors only for these actions.

operations.name: docx_read
operations.description: Read a canonical DOCX representation. complete returns one bounded cross-domain snapshot for broad small-document review; linear returns ordered blocks; structured returns hierarchy; domain returns one typed SDK domain. Always follow coverage and remainingReads until required scopes are complete.

maxChars.description: Aggregate text budget for package table-cell and section-content reads.

section.description: For section_content only: return section-relative block indices for retain.

readSnapshotId.description: Explicit revision-bound read snapshot returned by an earlier complete read. Reuse it with the next offset to avoid rebuilding every domain.

operations.name: docx_query
operations.description: Resolve deterministic, mutation-grade targets against the exact view. Use require=exactlyOne for a unique clause. Returned opaque targets can be passed to docx_apply arguments as selectorTarget.

operations.name: docx_apply
operations.description: Apply one action or workflow through a private candidate and durable receipt. Discover exact action arguments with docx_inspect.actions before first use; do not guess them. Reuse an opaque selectorTarget from query/read, or provide an inline select. Table workflows require a table selectorTarget or inline table select; use update_table_by_key for a row key and column header, including unmerged value cells in tables with unrelated merges. docx_inspect.workflowLimits states the supported shapes; do not guess cell coordinates after a refusal. Failed or partial engine receipts are never accepted.

action.description: One bounded high-level action. docx_inspect returns exact action help and the current supported catalogue.

arguments.description: Arguments for the selected action. Request its descriptor with docx_inspect.actions when needed; unknown or incomplete action arguments fail instead of being guessed.

selectorTarget.description: Opaque target returned by docx_query or a domain read. Query/read again after every mutation.

select.description: Inline selector resolved with require=exactlyOne. Prefer opaque targets when already available.

arguments.description: Arguments for the selected action. Request its descriptor with docx_inspect.actions when needed; unknown or incomplete action arguments fail instead of being guessed.

select.description: Inline selector resolved with require=exactlyOne against the step's current revision.

expectedText.description: Exact selected section body text, joined with newline; excludes the section heading. preserve stops before the first subsection; replace includes subsection headings/text.

readback.description: Optional bounded body text-block/table-cell changes with before/after text and fresh whole-block/table targets. maxChars is the total text budget. Preview has no reusable targets. Formatting, images and other stories/domains require explicit reads.

operations.name: docx_validate
operations.description: Validate an unpublished candidate without publishing it. Returns SuperDoc reopen and independent package evidence.

operations.name: docx_compare
operations.description: Compare the current source/candidate view with its opened source baseline using SuperDoc snapshots. Returns covered components and a structured change summary without modifying either document.

operations.name: docx_image_get
operations.description: Extract the exact PNG/JPEG bytes for an image target returned by docx_read(domain=images). Returns an owned asset and native MCP image content without executing embedded data.

operations.name: docx_export
operations.description: Publish the exact DOCX view as a PDF through configured LibreOffice. The result identifies the conversion engine and does not claim Microsoft Word layout fidelity. Repeating operationId recovers the same publication result.

operations.name: docx_save
operations.description: Validate and save a candidate returned by docx_apply or docx_create as a new DOCX without overwrite. An open source view alone is not a candidate: for an unchanged copy, first call docx_create with action=from_template and path. If a Save response is lost, use docx_operation_get with the original operationId; repeating identical Save arguments also recovers its receipt. The original is never changed.

operations.name: docx_close
operations.description: Close a DOCX handle and optionally discard unpublished candidates. Closing never deletes the source or a published output.

operations.name: docx_operation_get
operations.description: Recover a durable DOCX mutation or publication receipt by operationId. Use the same operation ID after an uncertain response; never invent a new ID for the same write.

layers.label: XLSX / CSV
layers.engine: Shared preserving OOXML service · Univer OSS 0.25.2 calculation · ExcelJS 4.4.0 creation · optional legacy Aspose.Cells
layers.summary: Read XLSX/CSV ranges and business keys. Apply atomic guarded cells through the same preserving service as the editor. XLSX additionally supports formulas, named tables, formatting, qualified row insertion, fill and sorting/filtering; CSV preserves literal fields and encoding.
layers.limitations: Opaque content is preserved. Special/shared formulas and unsafe numeric dependencies remain unresolved; protection and unsafe structural references are refused. No external-data refresh or chart/pivot authoring.
layers.proposedEngine: Ordinary supported XLSX workflows use local open-source calculation and the preserving writer. Aspose remains an explicit optional legacy route.

evaluation.summary: Shared open-source calculation and preserving edits cover bounded queries, guarded/keyed batches, qualified budget rows and save/reopen. Current actions and limits are documented in XLSX_MCP.md. Optional legacy Aspose routes are separate.

operations.name: xlsx_query
operations.description: Read a bounded XLSX or CSV range with reusable sheet/cell targets, literal values, stored raw values, formulas, caches and current calculation status. Set summary:true with sheet/range for native numeric statistics (no cell projection); keys and CSV summaries are not supported. Set search:{text,mode,after?} for bounded XLSX search; mode is display, raw or formula. Continue nextCursor until null; the match limit never drops results. Search cannot combine with keys, summary or offset. Omit sheet for inventory. CSV uses sheet CSV and literal text fields (including empty strings); it has no named tables, formulas or formatting. Example: {view,sheet:"Pricing",range:"A1:F20"}. XLSX uses local open-source calculation; unsupported dependencies remain unresolved.

coverage.description: Visited scope, completeness and explicit omissions.

wireTypes: content: text containing the same JSON

operations.name: xlsx_apply
operations.description: Apply one atomic batch to XLSX or CSV through the shared preserving service. Use returned view and a unique operationId; reused IDs recover the same result. XLSX supports cells/formulas, formatting, qualified budget rows, fill and sorting/filtering. Clear Hyperlinks uses canonical disjoint ranges and requires the native XLSX helper; it preserves cell content and formatting. CSV supports literal cells/setCells and updateRows by unique business keys with expected old values; values remain text and formula/format/structure commands are refused. CSV example: {sheet:"CSV",cell:"F2",expectedValue:"125",value:"150"}. Large receipt values may be omitted with explicit lengths/hashes; file contents remain complete. Failures publish nothing. Read the new view, then office_save to a new file with the original extension.
